title: Chai Before the Whistle
summary: Run a railway chai stall on AC: size the kettle coil, read a scope’s peak, time the brew and sync a camera to the phasor.
subject: physics
ncertRef: Section 7.2, AC voltage applied to a resistor
concepts: Resistance of a rated element, R = V²/P
Average power V_rms I_rms, never negative
Current in phase with voltage in a resistor
learningOutcome: The student can size a rated AC element with R = V²/P, convert between peak and rms values, find the energy from the average power, and read v and i in phase from a phasor.

levels.title: Wind the coil
levels.adds: Baseline: a rating is an rms value, so the coil needs R = V²/P; less resistance draws more than the rated current (Example 7.1).
hints: P = V²/R, so R = V²/P with V the rated rms voltage.
Less resistance means more current: the fuse allows only I = P/V.
More resistance means less power, and the train will not wait.

levels.title: Read the scope
levels.adds: New idea: a scope shows the peak value, and ratings use the rms value V = v_m/√2 (Ex 7.2).
hints: The scope shows the top of the wave, the peak v_m.
A selector set too low over-powers the coil; too high under-powers it.

levels.title: Brew on time
levels.adds: New idea: power in a resistor never goes negative and averages V²/R, half its peak, so the heat is (V²/R)·t (Ex 7.1).
hints: The average power is V_rms I_rms = V²/R.
Heat = average power × time, so t = E/P.
Using the peak power, twice the average, gives half the time and cold chai.

levels.title: Sync to the phasor
levels.adds: Apply it: v = v_m sin ωt and, in a resistor, i = i_m sin ωt in phase, with v_m = √2 V and i_m = √2 I (Section 7.3).
hints: Find the peak first: √2 times the rms value.
sin ωt = value ÷ peak, on the rising part of the wave.
In a resistor the current rises with the voltage, at the same angle.

misconceptions: The stated 220 V of the mains is the peak voltage
The average power in a resistor is zero over a cycle
The average power equals the peak power
The current in a resistor lags the voltage
